title: Cotton Club celebrity nights and who could get in
summary: The Cotton Club had a Black show and band but a White clientele, with Sunday celebrity nights, and Black patrons could get in if they could pay.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, they said people could come Uptown from Downtown with their furs and everything...
...and leave them in the car, and they'd still be there.

Oh yeah. The Cotton Club at that time, they entertained nothing but Hollywood celebrities. Sunday night was their Celebrity Night at the Cotton Club, and anybody who was ever a star in Hollywood, as soon as they'd come to New York, they would be at the Cotton Club that Sunday night.

To get their introduction. And I forget the fellow's name that used to be the MC there, but he knew ever star in Hollywood, and he would introduce them and this-that-and-the-other thing. It was just a meeting place for the stars. And they would come up here in Rolls-Royces and everything else. Nobody bothered them. No, they weren't ripped off at all.
Now, the Cotton Club was primarily for the Whit...
There was a White clientele, right?

It was definitely White, sure. But the place wasn't... The show and everything else was Negro. The band was Negro. But the club itself... Colored could go in there, Colored could go, but they... What the hell, they couldn't stand that tab. You know? You spend a lot of money.
So nobody would have been refused entrance.
Well, they might tell you the place is filled up or something like that, one of them things. But if you insisted on it, you could get in there. If you could prove that you had, you know...
Sure. Yeah, Bill Robinson used it for one of his hangouts, the Cotton Club.
And I imagine if Joe Louis wanted to go...
Well, he had no trouble going anywhere. You couldn't stop Joe Louis. He would have punched you in the nose! Heh-heh.

Yeah, Harlem used to be a beautiful place. You could go, and there were a lot of places to go and there was a lot of things you could see and do. It wasn't half-bad at all. Because it was a beautiful place. But things change. Everything changes. Well, it's deteriorated. It's not too
good now. It's not bad compared to a whole lot of places. But I mean, it's not the same. The feeling is not the same.
